video_title: Why Treasury Bonds Could Beat Stocks in 2027 | Keith McCullough
gist: Hedgeye's Keith McCullough argues the AI bubble peaked with CapEx and the 2026 economic cycle and is already crashing, with the economy heading into Quad 4 (growth and inflation slowing) in 1H 2027. He favors long Treasuries (10-year peaked at 5.31%, matching 2007), defensive sectors like utilities, staples and healthcare, and warns of widening credit spreads and a Fed tightening into the slowdown.

insights.claim: Keith McCullough declares the AI bubble is already crashing, defining a crash as a decline of more than 20% in a straight line, rather than a bubble that might burst in the future.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Treat AI leaders as in a bear phase now, not as a looming risk.
insights.quote: the AI bubble is crashing. I mean, I don't know what else to call it other than what happens when something goes down more than 20% in a straight line

insights.claim: McCullough argues the AI bubble peaked when AI CapEx and the economic cycle peaked in Q2 into Q3 2026, with semiconductors and South Korea's stock market peaking around the same time.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Peak CapEx rate-of-change marks the top for AI equities.
insights.quote: essentially the AI bubble peaked when CapEx peaked and the cycle peaked in the second quarter and into the third

insights.claim: Nvidia is down about 17% from its peak, about 3% from McCullough's 20% crash threshold, and broke trend on Hedgeye's signal in roughly the last week.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Nvidia, 8-9% of the S&P 500, is near joining the crash and drags passive 401k holders.
insights.quote: Nvidia, by the way, is down about 17% from where it it peaked. So, it's only 3% away from crashing.

insights.claim: Intel is described as a classic retail bag-holder stock that retail bought because the US government bought a stake, now down about 65% from where people own it.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Government-backed narratives do not protect retail entry prices.
insights.quote: It's down like 65% from where people own this thing.

insights.claim: McCullough calls AMD a crash stock that merely bounced off an oversold signal after a strong quarter, and says the key test is how it trades over the next three weeks, not three hours.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Judge post-earnings bounces in crashed names over weeks; failure confirms the bear.
insights.quote: AMD is a crash stock that just bounced

insights.claim: The Nasdaq has had an 8-10% drawdown from an all-time high set around the first week of October, which McCullough says is early days with much more downside possible.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Index-level damage likely lags component crashes; more drawdown expected.
insights.quote: I think these are early days.

insights.claim: McCullough's fractal framework says bubbles break first in components (semis, AI names) and the 'surface area' (Nasdaq, then S&P 500) caves in at the end.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Component crashes are a leading signal for index-level declines.
insights.quote: And then the surface area caves in at the end. The surface area is the Nasdaq and more broadly, it's certainly the S&P.

insights.claim: The most widely owned basket of retail brokerage stocks peaked at the end of May 2026, and many of those holdings have since collapsed.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Retail-favored baskets topped months before mega-cap indices.
insights.quote: Uh that that thing peaked at the end of May, okay?

insights.claim: Hedgeye has been short AI-financing-linked names such as CoreWeave, Nebius and Iron (as transcribed), which McCullough calls some of the best shorts of his life, and built an 'AI bubble cockpit' including their CDS to track the unwind.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Credit default swaps on AI neoclouds are a key gauge of AI bubble stress.
insights.quote: these are some of the best shorts of my life

insights.claim: McCullough says Hedgeye is short semiconductors and the AI bubble did not participate in the post-election relief rally, falling instead.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Divergence of AI names on an up day signals distribution.
insights.quote: Uh we're short semis, so it's a good day for that.

insights.claim: If the Democratic Congress cuts spending and curtails CapEx, McCullough says the AI bubble and the GDP boost from AI CapEx will not come back.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Policy-driven CapEx curtailment removes the main GDP and AI earnings driver.
insights.quote: you don't get your bubble and you don't get your bubble back if they cut CapEx spending

insights.claim: Disinflation in chip pricing would be terrible for semiconductor profits, part of a broader point that disinflation hurts the profit cycle.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Disinflationary quad hits earnings of inflation beneficiaries including chips.
insights.quote: what if we disinflate the pricing on chips? Is that good or bad? Terrible.

insights.claim: McCullough says the US economic cycle peaked in 2026 (GDP peaked) and the economy is about to enter Quad 4, in which rates of change of both growth and inflation slow simultaneously, expected in the first half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Position for growth and inflation slowing together in 1H 2027.
insights.quote: quad four is when the rate of change of both growth and inflation start to slow at the same time

insights.claim: McCullough claims Hedgeye's Quad 4 call has been undefeated and that Quad 4 predicts all stock market crashes.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Quad 4 regime shift is his core crash signal.
insights.quote: quad four predicts all stock market crashes

insights.claim: Current economic data is still in Quad 2 (growth and inflation accelerating), but markets are front-running the shift to Quad 4.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Markets rotate before the data confirms the quad change.
insights.quote: The market starts to front run the quad shift though.

insights.claim: A recession is not required for the bearish outcome; McCullough says only a slowdown in growth is needed.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Rate-of-change slowdown, not contraction, drives the trade.
insights.quote: you don't have to have a recession, you just have to have a slow down

insights.claim: Hedgeye is rotating from high-beta tech into healthcare, consumer staples and utilities (bought more utilities on the day), plus some financials, which it sees as a durable trend rather than a short trade.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Defensive low-beta sectors are the equity expression of Quad 4.
insights.quote: We bought more utilities today.

insights.claim: McCullough views healthcare and financial services as the two US sectors least disrupted and most establishment-run, making them a secular opportunity for AI-driven disruption and productivity (e.g. lab robots).
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: AI productivity gains may accrue most in healthcare and financials.
insights.quote: I actually think financial services and health care are are the two sectors of the US economy that have been disrupted the least.

insights.claim: Hedgeye exited its long shipping position before shipping stocks were cut in half repeatedly, citing BWET as the related ETF; inflation beneficiaries like energy and industrials suffer as inflation rolls over.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Exit inflation-beneficiary sectors as inflation cycle peaks.
insights.quote: BWET is ETF, uh, for that one.

insights.claim: McCullough places the 2026 AI bubble peak alongside the 2000 and 2007 cycle peaks as the three major cycle peaks in his roughly 30-year career.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Rare cycle peaks warrant large asset allocation shifts.
insights.quote: AI bubble peak is the 2026 peak

themes.theme: Long Treasuries as the big trade

insights.claim: McCullough says buying Treasury bonds is the most incremental asset allocation move now, having been short Treasuries earlier in the year; you buy bonds, not stocks, when growth and inflation slow.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Long-duration Treasuries are the top 2027 opportunity in his framework.
insights.quote: You don't go buy stocks when growth and inflation's slowing. You actually buy treasury bonds.

insights.claim: McCullough's signals say bond yields have peaked: the 10-year yield peaked at 5.31% in 2007 and, he says, peaked at the same 5.31% in 2026, implying big mean-reversion risk.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: A cycle peak in yields matching 2007 suggests a multi-year decline in yields.
insights.quote: guess what the 10-year yield peaked at in 2007? 5.31%.

insights.claim: After the 2007 cycle peak the 10-year yield fell to about 1.4% by 2012; McCullough suggests yields could drop 100 basis points, or even 300, within 6-9 months to years.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Substantial duration upside if the 2007 analog holds.
insights.quote: if the 10-year yield goes down 100 basis points, never never mind down 300 basis points

insights.claim: Falling oil would mainly relieve pressure on bond investors; Hedgeye was long oil until it broke its medium-term trade signal this week, and its next step would be to short oil and buy more bonds.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Oil breakdown reinforces the long-bond trade.
insights.quote: Next thing would be to short it and buy more bonds.

insights.claim: WTI remains bullish on Hedgeye's trend signal; a break below $92 would be like a dam breaking and could take WTI down $10-30.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: $92 WTI is the key level for a larger oil decline.
insights.quote: you'd have to break 92 on WTI which is our trend signal level

themes.theme: Credit spreads and a pro-cyclical Fed

insights.claim: McCullough says credit spreads bottom at the economic cycle peak and keep widening as the economy slows, so an AI-local credit event broadens into a general economic credit problem.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Expect spread widening to spread beyond AI issuers.
insights.quote: credit spreads bottom at the peak of the economic cycle, then start to widen

insights.claim: AI bubble financing is circular, and credit for those AI names essentially stopped trading, per McCullough.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: AI credit illiquidity is an early contagion warning.
insights.quote: Don't forget that this is circular financing.

insights.claim: High-yield spreads are around 330-340 basis points over Treasuries, which McCullough reads as a get-out signal because the cycle has peaked, not a post-election buy signal.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Widening HY spreads argue against risk-on.
insights.quote: we're at three 330 340 basis points over Treasuries right now in high yield

insights.claim: Hedgeye's weekly inflation nowcast predicted 3.74% last month to the basis point and expects two more months of acceleration to a high-3s inflation rate.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Near-term inflation prints likely hot, pressuring the Fed to tighten.
insights.quote: last last month we were looking for 3.74%. We nailed it right to a basis point.

insights.claim: McCullough believes the Fed's decision not to raise rates at its recent meeting was political ahead of the election, which forces it to tighten later, right into Quad 4 and a market crash.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Fed tightening into a slowdown raises crash risk.
insights.quote: if the Fed's tightening into a crash that's a really bad problem

insights.claim: Gold dislikes Quad 2 because the dollar and rates rise; Hedgeye has been bearish gold and is short silver.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Precious metals stay weak until the quad shift is confirmed by signals.
insights.quote: public enemy number one for something that has no yield, gold

insights.claim: From its cycle peak, gold was down 27% (as of the day before), silver down 57%, and palladium down even more, which McCullough calls crashes.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Precious metals have already crashed; don't buy the first bounce.
insights.quote: gold from its from its cycle peak was up until yesterday was down 27%

insights.claim: McCullough says he will get long gold again when the signal shifts, but not on the first bounce.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Wait for signal confirmation before re-entering gold.
insights.quote: You don't buy the first bounce.

insights.claim: McCullough sees SpaceX as the key stock to watch after Democrats swept Congress, arguing Elon Musk loses political power that helped SpaceX go public and get funding.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Political-connection premium in Musk-linked assets may unwind.
insights.quote: I think SpaceX is probably the best story to be paying attention to

insights.claim: The post-election rally was partly a squeeze from unwinding elevated pre-election S&P 500 put hedges, not a fundamental risk-on signal.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Fade hedge-unwind rallies.

insights.claim: McCullough says Trump was a catalyst for lower market volatility, but after the election loss volatility is breaking out because of a possible political phase transition.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Expect higher market volatility in the new political regime.
insights.quote: he was actually a catalyst for lower market volatility

insights.claim: Disinflation should relieve the bottom of the K-shaped economy while bludgeoning the wealthy top of the K through lost market cap, with Musk and SpaceX as the emblem.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Wealth effect reversal hits top-end consumption.

insights.claim: The triple-levered semiconductor ETF SOXL is down about 75% from June, having peaked near $25 billion AUM and lost $10 billion in three days, with its flows affecting market-on-close orders.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Leveraged retail ETF unwinds amplify semi selling.
insights.quote: It peaked at around 25 billion. It lost 10 billion in 3 days.

insights.claim: McCullough warns against being a 'macro tourist' who reacts to daily headlines like the election instead of focusing on where the economic cycle is.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Anchor decisions on cycle signals, not headlines.
insights.quote: you don't want to be a macro tourist

insights.claim: McCullough relies on signals built from the rate of change of price, volume and volatility because someone always has inside information, citing oil signals turning bullish before Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough
insights.so_what: Price/volume signals capture informed flows before news.
insights.quote: Somebody always knows something.
